group.name: Context-Aware Trustworthiness Assurance for AI Systems
group.definition: 고위험·공공·문화적 맥락에서 작동하는 AI 시스템이 안전성, 공정성, 설명가능성, 통제가능성을 유지하도록 평가하고 운영하는 기술이다. 모델과 에이전트의 실패 행동을 red-teaming·감사·배포 후 모니터링으로 확인하고, 인간 감독, 권한 통제, 공정성 검증, 도메인별 인증과 거버넌스 절차를 시스템에 결합한다. 순수한 agentic safety는 자율 에이전트의 행동 통제와 보안에, 순수한 fairness 연구는 집단별 편향 측정과 완화에 집중하는 반면, 이 기술군은 그러한 메커니즘을 실제 의료·금융·항공·공공·문화 환경의 운영 조건과 함께 보증하는 데 초점을 둔다.
group.evidence_summary: 여러 자료는 AI를 단순 예측 모델이 아니라 실제 업무와 사회 제도에 연결된 시스템으로 보고, 배포 환경에서 발생하는 유해 행동·불확실성·편향·책임 추적 문제를 반복해서 제기한다. 이에 대한 공통 해결 방식은 평가와 감사, red-teaming, 배포 후 모니터링, 인간 감독, 강건성·정렬 검증을 개발 과정과 운영 과정에 함께 넣는 것이다. 의료·금융·항공 사례에서는 인증과 규제·기관 수용성을 고려한 도메인별 검증이 강조되고, Global South·Muslim communities·비서구 환경 사례에서는 문화적 맥락과 대표성에 맞춘 fairness와 참여 설계가 강조된다. 에이전트 관련 자료는 이러한 보증 대상이 단일 모델에서 도구를 사용하고 상호작용하는 단일·다중 에이전트 시스템으로 확장되고 있음을 보여준다.
group.why_emerging: AI가 의료 진료, 금융 거래, 항공 안전, 법률 지원, 공공서비스와 정보 생태계에 직접 연결되면서 모델의 오류가 단순한 예측 오차를 넘어 운영·사회적 피해로 이어질 수 있게 되었다. 동시에 정적 모델보다 외부 도구를 사용하고 장기간 행동하며 다른 에이전트와 상호작용하는 시스템이 늘어나 기존의 사전 정확도 평가만으로는 실패를 확인하기 어려워졌다. 또한 여러 문화권과 취약 집단에 AI가 배치되면서 동일한 모델이라도 데이터 대표성, 공정성 기준, 인간 감독 방식이 달라지는 문제가 나타난다. 따라서 모델 수준의 안전 기법만이 아니라 배포 맥락에 맞춘 감사, 감독, 인증, 공정성 평가를 연결하는 기술이 필요해지고 있지만, 입력 자료는 이를 하나의 단일 메커니즘으로 수렴시키기보다는 여러 세부 축이 결합되는 과정을 보여준다.

claims.name: Multi-Agent AI Safety and Security
claims.evidence: Advanced AI systems are increasingly deployed as networks of interacting agents rather than as isolated models. Their most consequential failure modes are collective (Hammond et al., 2025; Schroeder de Witt et al., 2025).

claims.name: Trustworthy AI Evaluation and Red-Teaming
claims.evidence: Trustworthy AI models: evaluation, auditing, and red-teaming of models for harmful behaviors and failure modes; safety monitoring after deployment; and alignment and robustness methods.

claims.name: AI for Information Integrity
claims.evidence: AI for information integrity: detection and mitigation of disinformation, manipulation, and influence operations; and building resilience of the information ecosystem.

claims.name: Fairness-Aware AI for Marginalized Communities
claims.evidence: Algorithmic fairness and bias mitigation for equitable outcomes in marginalized communities

claims.name: Participatory and Human-Centered AI Design
claims.evidence: Human-AI collaboration and participatory AI design for local or community-driven contexts

claims.name: AI Dual-Use Governance Frameworks
claims.evidence: Dual-Use Attestations: A Verifiable Disclosure Primitive for Militarization-Risk Governance in ML Research

sources.title: Trustworthy AI for Good (AI4GOOD) Workshop @ ICML 2026

claims.name: Multi-Agent AI Safety and Security
claims.evidence: Advanced AI systems are increasingly deployed as networks of interacting agents rather than as isolated models. Their most consequential failure modes are collective (Hammond et al., 2025; Schroeder de Witt et al., 2025). Individually safe agents can jointly produce unsafe outcomes, and legitimate communication channels can be repurposed for covert coordination.

claims.name: Trustworthy and Aligned Foundation Models
claims.evidence: Trustworthy AI models: evaluation, auditing, and red-teaming of models for harmful behaviors and failure modes; safety monitoring after deployment; and alignment and robustness methods.

sources.title: 1st Workshop on Safe, Ethical, Certified, Uncertainty-aware, Robust, and Explainable AI for Health

claims.name: Trustworthy Clinical AI Systems
claims.evidence: As AI systems become increasingly integrated into healthcare workflows, we must ensure that they behave reliably under uncertainty, respect ethical constraints, and are interpretable to clinicians, patients, and regulators.

claims.name: Trustworthy and Deployable AI Systems
claims.evidence: Moving to a wider scope of deployment of the AI models into the real world is not just a simple question of translational research and engineering but also requires several fundamental research questions and issues, involving algorithmic, systemic and societal aspects, to be addressed.

claims.name: Trustworthy Agentic AI Systems
claims.evidence: Agentic AI marks a new frontier for artificial intelligence: systems that move beyond static prediction to autonomous reasoning, tool use, and sustained collaboration with humans and society.

claims.name: Fairness-Aware Environmental Machine Learning

claims.name: AI Safety and Security for Agentic Systems
claims.evidence: Our workshop provides the first dedicated venue for addressing the safety, security, and trustworthiness of agents in the wild.

claims.evidence: AI for Access to Justice AI systems that help people understand and exercise their legal right s Human - AI collaboration in legal workflows, self-help tools, and legal service Fairness, inclusion, accessibility, and the societal impact of legal AI

sources.title: Algorithmic Fairness Across Alignment Procedures and Agentic Systems

claims.name: Agentic Alignment and Fairness-Aware RLHF
claims.evidence: As the fairness challenges are fundamentally transformed by advanced AI systems, traditional algorithmic fairness frameworks developed primarily for prediction and/or prediction-based decision-making no longer suffice.

sources.title: Financial AI Security, Privacy, and Safety: Securing Real-World Financial AI Systems for Mission-critical Services including Fraud Detection, Anti-Money Laundering, Payments, and Bank Transfers

claims.name: Trustworthy Financial AI Systems
claims.evidence: This workshop examines the security, privacy, and safety challenges of AI systems deployed in financial services, with a focus on fraud detection, anti-money laundering, payments, and bank transfers. These systems operate on sensitive customer and transaction data in adversarial, regulated, and high-stakes environments. It brings together researchers, practitioners, regulators, and financial institutions to discuss how real-world financial AI systems can be designed, evaluated, governed, and deployed securely.

sources.title: Personalization in the Era of Large Foundation Models

claims.name: Trustworthy Personalized AI
claims.evidence: Safety, robustness, fairness, algorithmic bias across demographics, transparency in personalized decisions, privacy-preserving policies for personal data collection and storage, societal implications of widespread personalized AI deployment.

sources.title: The 3rd Workshop on LLMs and Generative AI for Finance

claims.name: Governance-Aware and Auditable AI for Finance
claims.evidence: The workshop moves beyond isolated model capabilities toward reliable institutional systems, covering agent orchestration, harness engineering, workflow-level evaluation, red teaming, retrieval and tool use, governance, auditability, model-risk management, and human-agent collaboration.

sources.title: Third Workshop on Agents in the Wild: Safety, Security, and Beyond

claims.name: Agentic AI Safety and Alignment
claims.evidence: As these systems increasingly reason, act, and adapt in open-ended environments, they raise fundamental challenges around safety, security, and trustworthiness, and recent developments have made these challenges increasingly urgent.

claims.name: Trustworthy AI for Aviation Safety
claims.evidence: Aviation Safety: The use of AI for enhancing aviation safety, but also the role of trustworthy AI in a high-stakes application domain.
